name: TWL World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The promotion's own top championship. Billed three-time champion Billy Joe McCallister lost it to his former Pain Incorporated partner Q-Ball at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view; a later broadcast recounts Q-Ball dropping the belt to the mat, vacating it, and quitting the promotion, and it remained vacant through the end of the surviving record.

name: TWL Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: Won by Palimetius the Historian at the promotion's own Helloween event by catching a dropped title belt off a ladder. He lost it to Sandman at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view; Sandman in turn lost it to XeRo at the promotion's own Armageddon event, the last title change recorded before the surviving record ends.

name: TWL Television Championship
epitaph: Billed the promotion's longest-held title under Adrian Blades, who retained it against Exodus at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view and against Prince Geatar on its own 21 February 1999 broadcast before a multi-man conspiracy cost him the belt to Dave Davidson at the promotion's own Armageddon event.

name: TWL Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Held by Chuckie Martinez entering 1999, who retained it against a recruited heavyweight at the promotion's own 26 January 1999 pay-per-view under the promotion's own rule barring a title change on a count-out. He later lost the title to Anthony Levert, who lost it in turn to El Puerco in a widely questioned finish at the promotion's own Armageddon event; Puerco retained it in a non-title four-corners bout ruled a no-contest on the promotion's own 3 May 1999 broadcast, the last card of the surviving record.

name: TWL World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Held by the pairing of Torture and XeRo entering 1999. The promotion's own president declared the titles vacant at its 26 January 1999 pay-per-view after Torture failed to appear for a scheduled defense and had XeRo assaulted and suspended on the same card; the tag team Sex Sells won the vacant championship in a title-deciding ladder match on the promotion's own 21 February 1999 broadcast and were still billed champions at the end of the surviving record.
